note: Settings > AI brain: a Link and a Prompt button per provider. 'link' opens in the browser. 'prompt' is copied for the player to give to a coding agent. {game_dir}, {user_dir} and {config_file} are filled in with this machine's real paths when the button is pressed. 'prompt_intro' is shown above the prompt; its example folder is only an example.
prompt_intro: Give this to a coding agent with access to the internet and your computer, in a trusted location (e.g. ~/projects/desert-spaceport).

ollama.title: Ollama
ollama.prompt:
Set up Ollama as the AI brain for my game, Desert Spaceport. Work on this computer and tell me before anything that needs my password.

1. Install Ollama from https://ollama.com/download (on macOS, `brew install ollama` also works) and make sure it is running. Check with `curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags`; it should answer with JSON.
2. Pull a model that fits this machine's memory. Check the RAM first. 16 GB or more: `ollama pull qwen3:30b-a3b`. Less than that: `ollama pull qwen3:4b-instruct`. Tell me which one you picked and why.
3. Run `ollama run <model> "say you are ready"` once to prove it answers.
4. The game keeps its settings in {config_file} (create it if it does not exist; keep any JSON already in it). Merge in only this, with the model name you pulled:
   {"ai_enabled": true, "profiles": {"ollama": {"model": "<model>"}}}
   Do not touch anything else in that file. The game reads it field by field on top of its own defaults ({game_dir}/content/core/llm/defaults.json).
5. Tell me to open the game, press F10, set Mode to ollama (or auto) and press Test. Report what you installed, the model, and where the config is.

Do not install anything else, and do not send anything off this machine.

local.title: Local server (llama.cpp)
local.prompt:
Set up llama.cpp's llama-server as the local AI brain for my game, Desert Spaceport. Work on this computer and tell me before anything that needs my password.

1. Install llama.cpp. On macOS: `brew install llama.cpp`. On Windows or Linux: download the latest release build for this machine from https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases (pick the GPU build that matches my hardware if there is one) and put `llama-server` somewhere stable. Confirm with `llama-server --version`, and tell me the full path to the binary.
2. Download a GGUF model into {game_dir}/runtime/models/ and name it cantina_owner.gguf (the game also uses any .gguf in that folder). Check the RAM first. 16 GB or more: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf (about 18 GB). Less than that: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf (about 2.5 GB). Tell me which one you picked and why, and check there is enough free disk first.
3. Prove it works: start `llama-server --model <that file> --port 8088 --jinja -ngl 99`, wait for `curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/health` to say ok, send one request to http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions, then stop the server. The game starts and stops it itself.
4. The game keeps its settings in {config_file} (create it if it does not exist; keep any JSON already in it). Merge in only this:
   {"ai_enabled": true}
   and, only if the binary is not at /opt/homebrew/bin/llama-server or on the PATH, also {"profiles": {"local": {"sidecar": {"bin": "<full path to llama-server>"}}}}. The game reads it field by field on top of its own defaults ({game_dir}/content/core/llm/defaults.json), and also looks in $LLAMA_SERVER, {game_dir}/runtime/bin/ and the PATH.
5. Tell me to open the game, press F10, set Mode to local (or auto) and press Test. Report what you installed, the model, the binary path, and where the config is.

Do not install anything else, and do not send anything off this machine.

cloud.title: Cloud (Claude API)
cloud.prompt:
Help me set up a cloud AI key as the brain for my game, Desert Spaceport. Work on this computer, and read this whole message before doing anything.

1. Open https://platform.claude.com in my browser and ask me to sign in, add billing if it needs it, and create an API key (it starts with sk-ant-). I must do the sign-in, the billing and the key myself. Do not create an account, enter payment details, or ask me to paste the key into this chat.
2. Never print, log or commit the key. The easiest safe route: tell me to open the game, press F10, paste the key into "Cloud key", turn on "Cloud enabled", set Mode to cloud (or auto), and press Save then Test. Pasting an sk-ant- key sets the URL, type and model for Anthropic automatically, and the game stores the key in {user_dir}/llm/keys.cfg, never in the project.
3. If I would rather use an environment variable than the settings screen, show me how to set DUNE_LLM_KEY in my shell profile for my own shell, and let me paste the value there myself.
4. The game keeps its other settings in {config_file}. If AI characters are still off, merge {"ai_enabled": true} into that file (create it if needed, keep any JSON already in it) or tell me to switch on "AI characters" in F10. The game's defaults are in {game_dir}/content/core/llm/defaults.json.
5. Tell me to expect a small per-use cost on my own account, and that I can set a spend limit in the console.

Do not install anything and do not store the key in any file inside the game folder.
